text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The strike staged by members of the national carrier Kenya Airways ends after a seven-point tripartite agreement is reached by all parties.

- The outgoing chairman of the Public Investment Committee Professor Peter Anyang' Nyongo criticises the government for failing to rationalise its privatisation programme and for its inability to punish those who have mismanaged State corporations.
- Decommissioned mv St Michael, a 40-year-old ferry, lists and sinks 500 metres from the scene of the 1994 Mtongwe ferry disaster. No loss of life.
- President Daniel arap Moi secures release of an Australian pilot, Justin Fraser, from captivity in Somalia.

- Multinational food company Nestle Foods Kenya denies claims that it is lobbying to take over the marketing of all dairy products after purchasing some factories owned by the giant Kenya Cooperative Creameries.
- An enraged husband stabs a man to death after allegedly catching him red-handed making love to his wife.
- Kenya is given a clean bill in its human rights record by a joint assembly of the Carribean and Pacific countries and the European Union.

- The operations of cash strapped Nzoia Company, which produces sugar, are paralysed by an employee strike and a vow by cane farmers never to take their produce to the company unless they are paid for cane delivered to the factory.
- Ketan Somaia's Dolphin Group is exploring investment opportunities on the Indian Ocean Seychelles island of Seychelles.
